title: Pythagorean walks on $\mathbb{Z}^2$
summary: We consider an infinite graph with the vertex set $\mathbb{Z}^2$ and edges connecting the vertices iff the Euclidean distance between the respective points is an integer, and the points do not lie on the same horizontal or vertical. Equivalently, there must exist a Pythagorean triangle with the hypotenuse corresponding to the graph edge and the legs parallel to the axes. We prove that the diameter of this graph is $3$, but surprisingly it appears that the nodes at the maximal (graph) distance of $3$ apart seem to be only those that are geometrically very close to each other.
